about: Arts, books, food and traditions 'Did you know?' facts.
items: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.
The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
Bonfire Night marks the failure of the Gunpowder Plot on 5 November 1605.
Queen Victoria and Prince Albert helped make Christmas trees popular in Britain.
Fish and chips have been sold together in Britain since at least the 1860s.
The British Museum, founded in 1753, was the first national public museum in the world.
Vincent van Gogh sold very few paintings during his lifetime.
Jane Austen's novels were first published anonymously.
The Edinburgh Festival Fringe, founded in 1947, is the world's largest arts festival.
Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.
The first Notting Hill Carnival street festival took place in 1966.
Afternoon tea is credited to Anna, Duchess of Bedford, in the 1840s.
Paddington Bear first appeared in the book A Bear Called Paddington in 1958.
